chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Papa Stoppa and Senator LeBlanc want to thank Danny for the Hadacol jingle
summary: A disc jockey played the Hadacol lyric repeatedly, and the senator, who sold Hadacol, invited Danny to receive a present.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: [DANNY BARKER PLAYS SOME MORE, AND THEY PERFORM]
[AS SONG ENDS]... then I'd go into dance(?).
So they were playing it around here. So that's why Paul wrote and told Danny "Come on back down here..."
So went to Louisiana. I had never been nowhere in Louisiana before. So we went with this record being out -- and in Texas, see.
The Hadicol(?) man. We sent it to Dudley Lebeau. He was a Louisiana State Senator who had a patent
medicine. And they had this medicine, he had publicized it, and he used to sell it like it was taking an antiseptic.

But it wasn't all over before then. I'll tell you what happened. It wasn't all over then. He would say, "She can drink a lot of Hadicol," "Oh, no, she can't," "Oh yes, she can." You had a disk jockey here named Papa Stoppa(?) who used to take just that part when he was publicizing the Hadicol(?) thing. "You know, you can do a lot of Hadicol..." -- and he'd play that over and over and over and over, see.

So somebody found out I was here. So they sent for me, and they said, "Senator Lebeau wants to see you. He wants to thank you for making that record." Because they wanted to get off the hook, because I guess the government was suing them for using that as a gimmick. So he said, "Senator Lebeau..." He called me, Papa Stoppa. He said, "Hey, Danny Barker?" I said, "Yeah." He said, "I want to see you. Come down to my office at the hotel, the Louisiana(?) Hotel. I want to see you and I want to talk to you." He said, "Senator Dudley Lebeau wants to see you. He's coming to town next week; he has a present for you."
He was supposed to give me a watch.
"He appreciates this thing. He's been looking for a jingle, and he's finally found something that's perfect for his Hadicol program." He said, "When he comes in town, I'll call you."
